title: introduce-commitlet-oracle-and-throttle-negotiator
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: Dedicated fleets currently allocate capacity using coarse reservation windows (minutes-to-hours). For bursty tenants this leads to either over-provisioning or repeated emergency fallback to cheaper model variants. Motivation: Introduce a lightweight per-tenant micro-reservation primitive ("commitlet") plus a cross-pool negotiation agent that dynamically brokers transient throughput across sibling pools when headroom is available. Goals: 1) Improve tail throughput for short-lived bursts without enlarging long-term reservations. 2) Provide a predictable, auditable accounting unit for transient allocations. 3) Keep latency impact negligible and keep scheduler complexity bounded.

What this PR does: Adds a Commitlet Oracle service that issues timeboxed micro-commitments (commitlets) backed by an elastic safety credit. Commitlets are small (tokenized) allocations that attach to incoming requests and are consumable for a short window (30s–5min). A new Throttle Negotiator module coordinates soft transfers between pools: when one pool has spare tokens it publishes a transferable budget; neighboring pools can claim up to a configured fraction subject to SLO guardrails. The Negotiator prefers local warmlets and prefers cross-pool transfers only when local latency headroom is observed.

Implementation notes: - New service pkg/autoscale/commitlet_oracle.go with a minimal in-memory ledger + persistent tombstone store for idempotency. - Negotiator implemented under pkg/orchestrator/throttle_negotiator.go exposing a gRPC API used by pool controllers. - Control plane: small additions to control-plane API (v2) for commitlet issuance and redemption; backward compatibility preserved: pools without the feature will ignore the new fields. - Metrics & telemetry: commitlet_issue_count, commitlet_redeem_latency_ms, crosspool_transfer_attempts, negotiated_transfer_success_rate. - Config: feature gated behind operator flag --enable-commitlets and per-tenant quota caps.

Migration and rollout: Workload-safe by default: commitlets disabled on old clusters. Rolling upgrade plan in docs: install operator flag, enable commitlets in a single staging pool, run smoke + synthetic burst profile, gradually enable on production pools with progressive quota. A migration job will backfill any missing tombstones in the oracle store but is conservative (no retroactive accounting changes).

Testing and validation: Unit tests for ledger and negotiator state machine. Integration harness uses benchlab synthetic bursts (see tests/integration/commitlet_oracle_test.go) to validate that 95th/99th percentile throughput improves for burst traces while p99 latency impact is <5ms for the runway cases. A canary run on a subset of Dedicated fleet (us-west-2) showed a median cost delta of +0.8% with 18% fewer fallback events for targeted tenants.

Backward compat: No breaking API changes. Config default is off. Operators must opt in and set per-tenant caps to avoid unbounded spend.

Related: ENG-3419 (commitlet design), PM-504 (product requirements), incident SUP-1120 (context for emergency fallbacks).
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial oracle and negotiator prototypes; add control-plane API v2 extensions; ledger persistence and tombstone backfill; metrics and dashboards; integration test harness; docs and operator flag. Each commit is focused and namespaced to relevant packages.
ci_checks: integration: flaky - rerun required (1 failure on first run, rerun passed)
review_conversation: Jonah Kim (2025-08-14): Nice design. Two requests: add a fast-path for local warmlet claiming and clarify tombstone retention policy.
Maya Patel (2025-08-15): Added fast-path in throttle_negotiator.go and documented tombstone retention (14 days, configurable).
Lina Gómez (2025-08-20): Request change - need additional unit test for double-issue prevention when oracle restarts mid-window.
Maya Patel (2025-08-22): Added ledger restart test and a small refactor to make state writes idempotent. Updated tests/integration accordingly.
Arjun Desai (2025-08-28): Verified metrics and load characteristics in local canary; left a minor nits comment on variable naming (fixed).
Lina Gómez (2025-09-01): Approved after tests and docs updates.
release_notes: Introduces Commitlet Oracle and Throttle Negotiator (opt-in). - New micro-reservation primitive (commitlet) for short-lived burst throughput. - Cross-pool soft transfers mediated by Throttle Negotiator. - Metrics: commitlet_issue_count, commitlet_redeem_latency_ms, crosspool_transfer_attempts. Operator action: enable with --enable-commitlets and set per-tenant caps.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: misconfigured caps could allow transient spend increases or affect fairness. Mitigations: feature is off by default, per-tenant caps and global safety credit, audit logs captured for every transfer, canary rollout guidance provided in docs.
testing: Unit + integration + benchlab. Integration showed improved burst throughput with limited cost impact in canary. Ran synthetic burst profiles from benchlab (config bspec/short_burst.yaml). No regression observed on existing autoscaler unit tests.
performance_impact: Microbenchmark: commitlet issuance adds ~0.6ms median to request control-plane path; negotiated transfers are asynchronous and do not affect request latency directly. End-to-end p99 latency impact observed <5ms in canary for typical request sizes.
notes_for_oncall: If operators see a large number of 'transfer_rejected_quota' events, verify tenant cap configuration and global safety credit level. Tombstone backfill job may show transient I/O pressure; backfill runs at low priority. To emergency-disable: set --enable-commitlets=false and drain commitlet queues via the operator endpoint.
changelog_entry: feat(autoscaler): add commitlet oracle + throttle negotiator (opt-in)
